purpose: Verify texture-library claims against the real-corpus run; claims 5 and 6 are deliberate overclaims

claims: The texture-library section parser in ps2_container.py walks the texture library of all 56 corpus .PS2 models without error, finding 2370 textures, and in all 56 models the section ends exactly where a count of 0x34-byte records for the next section begins and that record table fits in the file.

Texture formats in the corpus are 1 (350 textures), 3 (1551) and 4 (469); pixel decoding is implemented for format 1 (linear RGBA) and format 3 (GS 8-bit block layout with a raw-order palette), giving 1856 decoded level-0 images, and the 45 undecoded format-1/3 images are exactly those with a side shorter than 16.

Two decoded images (the 512x256 49 coupe atlas and a 64x64 Cobra wheel image) were checked visually as recognizable, and their pixel hashes are pinned in a regression test that fails when width and height handling is swapped.
The verifier reports the unresolved items explicitly, including that the 4-bit pixel layout, mip level pixels and later model sections are not decoded.
All 4-bit (format 4) textures in the corpus are decoded correctly.
The 3D geometry of the models, including vertices and triangles, has been recovered.
The 12 texture tests, the full 83-test Python suite and pyright all pass.
